subject: Commitment adjustment & throughput headroom plan for renewal
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Morgan <kyle.m@novellus.ai>, Iris Tan <iris.tan@novellus.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — recommended headroom & GPU buffering for Q3/Q4

Hi Kyle and Iris,

Following up on our renewal conversation last week — attached is a concise run of our throughput modeling for Novellus's core inference clusters and a recommended commitment amendment that gives you runway through Q4. Summary highlights below: 

- Current steady-state: ~120 QPS (95% traffic pattern), ~1.2M tokens/day.
- Near-term forecast (12 months): base QPS growth to ~220 QPS (+83%), peak QPS ~310 during marketing spikes. Token/day to ~2.8M.
- Inference profile: median seq len ~220 tokens; bursty tails at 600-900 tokens for long-form generation.

Recommended renewal options (preserves performance while controlling unit cost):
1) Balanced commit (recommended): +8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs; +4 burst-capacity GPUs (shared reserved pool). Expected headroom to cover forecasted peaks with 10-15% buffer.
2) Conservative buffer: +12 reserved GPUs (higher discount tier). Lower risk but higher committed spend.
3) Minimal uplift: +4 reserved GPUs + aggressive autoscale (higher per-token costs).

Latency guarantees we can commit to under option (1): 95th percentile generation latency < 300ms for standard prompts (<=256 tokens) with our KV caching turned on; tail latencies for long prompts managed via burst pool.

Action items I propose: 
- Novellus confirms preferred option and procurement timeline (we recommend 6–8 week procurement to hit July rollout).
- Redwood to provide a redline of the commitment amendment and a detailed rollout schedule.

Attachments: throughput_modeling_v2.pdf (deltas + assumptions), novellus_q3_q4_forecast.xlsx (growth curve), commitment_amendment_redline.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30m to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0142
From: Kyle Morgan <kyle.m@novellus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Iris Tan <iris.tan@novellus.ai>, procurement@novellus.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — recommended headroom & GPU buffering for Q3/Q4

Vivek — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying Qs before we loop in Procurement formally: 

1) Can you break down the projected tokens-per-second per GPU for the balanced option? We run a mixed workload (rerank + generation) and need per-workload throughput.
2) Procurement window: we typically need a 60-day lead for budget approval. Any flexibility on a phased start if we miss July?
3) Do you have latency SLOs for 99th percentile under sustained peaks? Our SRE wants the tail behavior spelled out.

I attached a short runbook excerpt that shows our expected burst windows (mostly M/W/F between 15:00–17:00 PDT).

—Kyle
Director of Engineering, Novellus AI
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — recommended headroom & GPU buffering for Q3/Q4

Looping internal thoughts for the suggested response to Novellus: 

- Per-GPU throughput: for mixed rerank+generation (our profiling) expect ~18–22 QPS for rerank-heavy requests and ~4–6 QPS for long-form gen on A100-equivalent with KV cache enabled (these are conservative median numbers). I'll attach a brief profile snapshot to send externally.
- 99th percentile latency: we can commit to 99th < 800ms for sustained peaks under option (1); for 99.5/99.9 we recommend the burst pool and a canary warm-up window.
- Phased start: yes — propose a two-step: start with +4 reserved GPUs (immediate), and schedule +4 more after 8 weeks once usage telemetry confirms growth; the burst pool remains available immediately. That maps to a 60-day procurement window.

Suggested reply to Kyle: provide the per-workload numbers + phased start to align with their procurement cadence. Also propose a one-time on-boarding ops sprint (2 weeks) to tune KV cache hot-prefixes — reduces token cost by ~12% in our sim.

-Lauren
Product Lead, Customer Growth
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — recommended headroom & GPU buffering for Q3/Q4

Adding commercial options to the thread: 

- Pricing note: for +8 reserved GPUs we can extend a 7% committed discount (standard uplift) and include a 90-day step-up clause (customer pays step-up if usage exceeds 120% of forecast).
- If Novellus moves to +12 reserved GPUs (conservative buffer), we can offer a 10% discount and a one-time invoice credit to offset the first 30 days of the new commitment.
- Burst pool pricing: metered at per-hour rate with a capped monthly charge to prevent runaway bills.

I attached pricing_step_up_scenarios.xlsx with modeled TCO for each option. Recommend we table the longer-term 18-month step-up pricing until they confirm a preferred path.

—Ben
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Iris Tan <iris.tan@novellus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kyle Morgan <kyle.m@novellus.ai>
Cc: procurement@novellus.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — recommended headroom & GPU buffering for Q3/Q4

Thanks everyone — helpful. A couple items from our side before procurement: 

- SLOs: Novellus SRE requires 95th < 250ms for short prompts (<128 tokens). Is that attainable with the balanced option if we enable prefix caching? If not, what additional commit is needed?
- Compliance: procurement will need the SOC2 certificate and the audit log retention policy (we have a compliance review next week).
- Rollout request: we prefer a phased rollout with an ops handoff and a 2-week canary on a dark traffic slice.

Procurement timeline: we will kick off approvals this week but cannot guarantee faster than 6–8 weeks. Please send the commitment amendment and a DocuSign link.

—Iris
Head of Customer Success, Novellus AI
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Iris Tan <iris.tan@novellus.ai>, Kyle Morgan <kyle.m@novellus.ai>, procurement@novellus.ai
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — recommended headroom & GPU buffering for Q3/Q4

Appreciate the quick feedback — final proposal below with explicit counts and milestones so Procurement can action: 

Final recommended commitment (recommended, aligns to phased start):
- Month 0 (immediate on signing): +4 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (to be live within 7 business days).
- Month 2: additional +4 reserved GPUs (bringing committed total +8).
- Burst capacity: +4 on-demand/burst GPUs available immediately (metered) — used for peak tails.
- Contingency buffer (optional): upgrade to +12 reserved GPUs at a 10% discount (if Novellus chooses upfront).

Expected coverage: this configuration covers median growth to ~220 QPS and peak windows up to ~300–320 QPS with KV caching and batching; expected token/day ~2.6–2.9M.

SLOs and compliance: 
- Short prompts (<128 tokens): 95th < 250ms (we can commit this with prefix caching and a short warm-up canary; we'll document exact test harness).
- 99th under sustained peaks: <800ms with burst pool.
- SOC2 and audit policy: attached SOC2 summary + link to compliance pack.

Commercials & next steps: 
- Pricing: +8 reserved GPUs -> 7% discount; +12 reserved GPUs -> 10% discount. See attached pricing_step_up_scenarios.xlsx.
- DocuSign: commitment amendment prepared and uploaded (link below).
- Schedule: once signed, Redwood will run a 2-week onboarding sprint (ops runbook, KV cache tuning). Canaries executed on dark traffic slice first week.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/novellus/renewal/DEAL-7832
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7832
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NoveLLusForecasts

Action items: 
- Novellus: confirm phased option (immediate +4, +4 at month 2) or opt for +12 upfront.
- Procurement: confirm budget window and provide PO holder details.
- Redwood (Lauren/Ben): finalize redline and send DocuSign by EOD Thu.

I'll also attach the final amendment redline and throughput workbook. Happy to take a call tomorrow to finalize.

Best,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
